questions.question_text:
Car $E$'s fuel-use graph and car $F$'s fuel-use graph both pass through the origin. Car $E$'s gradient is $0.03$ L/km and car $F$'s gradient is $0.09$ L/km.
What is the ratio of car $F$'s fuel-use rate to car $E$'s fuel-use rate?

options.why: Inverted the ratio direction, comparing $E$ to $F$ instead of $F$ to $E$ as asked.
Subtracted the two gradients ($0.09 - 0.03$) instead of dividing them.
Made an arithmetic slip dividing $0.09$ by $0.03$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{0.09}{0.03}$
$= 3$
Car $F$'s fuel-use rate is $3$ times car $E$'s, so the ratio is $3:1$.
